questions.0.explain.t: Without evals, every prompt or model change is a guess.

questions.0.options.0.t: Measuring the quality of the AI system with repeatable test cases

questions.0.options.1.t: Training the model with the test cases that failed

questions.0.options.2.t: Encrypting the prompts sent to the model

questions.0.options.3.t: Reducing the context size on each round

questions.1.explain.t: Synthetic cases lose the real distribution; real ones show where the system truly fails.

questions.1.options.0.t: Because they reflect how users actually use the system

questions.1.options.1.t: Because they are cheaper than creating synthetic test cases

questions.1.options.2.t: Because they remove any human review of the results

questions.1.options.3.t: Because the model requires real data to work

questions.1.q.t: Why use real production data in evals?

questions.2.explain.t: Evaluating each stage (retrieval, generation, tools) locates the cause.

questions.2.options.0.t: You do not know whether the failure came from retrieval, the prompt or the model

questions.2.options.1.t: It becomes too expensive to run on every change

questions.2.options.2.t: The final answer may simply not exist

questions.2.options.3.t: It is not possible to measure anything without looking at the internal steps

questions.2.q.t: What is the problem with evaluating only the final answer?
